experiences.name: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel
experiences.description: Explore one of the world's greatest art collections, culminating in Michelangelo's breathtaking Sistine Chapel ceiling. Book skip-the-line tickets in advance to maximize your time among thousands of masterpieces spanning centuries of artistic achievement.

experiences.name: Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk
experiences.description: Wander through the cobblestone streets of Trastevere sampling supplì (fried rice balls), artichokes alla romana, fresh pasta, and local Frascati wine at family-run trattorias and street food stalls. This bohemian neighborhood offers the most authentic Roman culinary experience away from tourist traps.

experiences.name: Borghese Gallery Art Tour
experiences.description: Visit this intimate yet world-class gallery housing Bernini's stunning sculptures and Caravaggio's dramatic paintings inside a baroque villa. Reservations are mandatory and entry is limited to 360 visitors at a time, ensuring an unhurried, immersive experience with masterpieces like Apollo and Daphne.

experiences.name: Testaccio Market & Offal Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive deep into Rome's culinary soul at the Mercato Testaccio, the city's most authentic covered food market. Sample porchetta sandwiches, aged pecorino romano, cured meats, and the famously divisive quinto quarto (offal dishes) that define true Roman cucina povera tradition.

experiences.name: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Archaeological Walk
experiences.description: Stroll through the ancient heart of the Roman Empire across the Forum and Palatine Hill, where emperors once lived. Combined with Colosseum entry, this archaeological complex offers unparalleled insight into Roman history and culture, with panoramic views over ruins that inspired Renaissance artists for centuries.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Rome
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 16:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Rome, GA airport at 16:00 on Condor flight. Collect luggage, arrange ground transport, and check in to La Quinta by Wyndham Rome at 15 Chateau Drive. Freshen up and get oriented in the local area around the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Take a relaxed evening stroll around the Chateau Drive neighborhood to get your bearings. Visit a nearby grocery store (Walmart or Kroger on Shorter Ave) to stock up on snacks, breakfast items, and drinks to save money throughout the trip — a key budget travel hack.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight or airport snacks
meals.lunch: Meal on the flight or airport food court
meals.dinner: Zaxby's or Taco Bell on Shorter Ave NW — quick, filling, and budget-friendly options within a short drive of the hotel (~$8–12 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Rome, GA (not Rome, Italy) is the destination based on the hotel address (34.2212, -85.1513). Keep Day 1 light — rest is important after travel. Set an early alarm for Day 2 to maximize sightseeing. Average high of ~30°C means stay hydrated and wear light clothing.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Rome Area History Museum (401 Broad St, Rome, GA) — free or low-cost admission. Explore exhibits on the history and culture of the Rome, GA area. Arrive early (~9:00 AM) to beat the heat. The museum is housed in a historic Carnegie Library building and is a great introduction to the city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Myrtle Hill Cemetery (just off Broad St) — a stunning hilltop cemetery with panoramic views of Rome's three rivers and rolling hills. Free to visit. Afterward, walk along the Riverwalk along the Oostanaula River for a scenic, shaded stroll. Explore the public art installations and murals along Broad Street downtown — Rome has a growing street art scene perfect for art lovers.
day_by_day.evening: Explore downtown Rome's Broad Street in the cooler evening hours. Browse local shops and admire the historic architecture. Visit the iconic Clock Tower at the intersection of Broad and 5th Ave for a photo opportunity.

meals.breakfast: Use groceries purchased last night — cereal, fruit, or yogurt from the hotel room to save money (~$2–3)
meals.lunch: Harvest Moon Cafe on Broad St — local favorite with affordable sandwiches and salads (~$10–14 per person)
meals.dinner: El Sombrero Mexican Restaurant on Shorter Ave — generous portions, authentic flavors, very budget-friendly (~$10–13 per person)

day_by_day.notes: With a high of ~30°C, plan outdoor activities in the morning and evening. Carry a reusable water bottle. Wear sunscreen. Downtown Rome is very walkable — save on transport by parking once and exploring on foot.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Berry College (2277 Martha Berry Hwy NW) — one of the most beautiful college campuses in the US and completely free to visit. Explore the stunning Gothic architecture, the historic Ford Buildings, and the vast natural grounds. Art lovers will appreciate the architectural beauty and the serene landscape. Arrive by 9:00 AM before the heat peaks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Oak Hill & The Martha Berry Museum on the Berry College campus (small admission fee ~$5). Explore the historic home and gardens of Martha Berry, founder of the college. Afterward, drive to the Rome Area Council for the Arts or check out any local gallery exhibitions on Broad Street — many are free to enter.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free outdoor event or community gathering if available (check Rome's local events calendar at romega.us). Otherwise, enjoy a sunset walk at the Oostanaula River Riverwalk — beautiful golden hour light over the water.

meals.breakfast: Hotel room breakfast with groceries (~$2–3)
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch at Berry College — pack sandwiches and snacks from grocery store items (~$4–5 per person)
meals.dinner: Schroeder's New Deli on Broad St — a Rome institution with hearty, affordable deli sandwiches and soups (~$9–12 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Berry College has free roaming deer on campus — a delightful surprise for visitors. The campus spans 27,000 acres, so wear comfortable walking shoes. Check Berry College's public visitor guidelines before going.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Coosa Valley — drive to the Lock and Dam Park in Rome (free entry) along the Coosa River. Enjoy the scenic riverside views, walking trails, and wildlife. Great for photography and nature appreciation. Arrive early (~8:30 AM) for cooler temperatures and better wildlife sightings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Chieftains Museum / Major Ridge Home (501 Riverside Pkwy NE) — a National Historic Landmark and one of Rome's most significant cultural sites. Admission is low-cost (~$5–7). The museum tells the story of the Cherokee Nation and Major Ridge, with fascinating art and artifacts. A must-visit for history and art enthusiasts.
day_by_day.evening: Return to downtown Rome for the evening. Browse the local farmers market if it's running (check local schedule). Enjoy the cooler evening temperatures with a walk along Broad Street and window shopping.

meals.breakfast: Hotel room breakfast with groceries (~$2–3)
meals.lunch: Subway or Jimmy John's near Riverside Pkwy — quick, affordable, and customizable (~$8–10 per person)
meals.dinner: Partridge Restaurant on Broad St or a local pizza spot — look for daily specials and happy hour deals (~$12–15 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Chieftains Museum may have limited hours — call ahead or check their website. June 19 is Juneteenth, a federal holiday, so some venues may have special events or altered hours. Stay hydrated throughout the day.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Rome Little Theatre or check for any morning art workshops or community art events in Rome. Visit the Shorter University Art Gallery (315 Shorter Ave) — free to visit and features rotating exhibitions by students and regional artists. A wonderful hidden gem for art lovers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Cave Spring, GA (~15 miles southwest of Rome) — a charming small town with a natural limestone cave (Rolater Park, ~$3 admission) and a beautiful spring-fed swimming pool. Explore the historic downtown, antique shops, and the cave. A unique and very affordable afternoon adventure.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Rome for a relaxed evening. Visit a local ice cream shop or dessert spot on Broad Street to cool down after the warm day. Enjoy the vibrant downtown atmosphere as locals come out in the cooler evening hours.

meals.breakfast: Hotel room breakfast with groceries (~$2–3)
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch for Cave Spring — sandwiches, fruit, and drinks from grocery store (~$4–5 per person)
meals.dinner: Amici Italian Restaurant in Rome — authentic Italian-inspired dishes at reasonable prices, fitting the food interest theme (~$13–16 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Cave Spring is a short, easy drive from Rome and well worth the trip. Bring a light jacket for inside the cave — temperatures are cooler underground. The swimming pool at Rolater Park is a great way to cool off on a hot June day (small fee may apply).

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel experience — based on the available experience listed, explore this world-class art collection featuring Michelangelo's breathtaking Sistine Chapel ceiling. Book tickets in advance online to save time and potentially get discounted rates. Arrive at opening time to avoid crowds (~$20–25 for standard admission).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Vatican Museums' vast galleries — the Gallery of Maps, Raphael Rooms, and the Pinacoteca art gallery. Take your time in the Sistine Chapel to fully absorb Michelangelo's masterpiece. Visit St. Peter's Basilica (free entry) afterward for its stunning Renaissance art and architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Reflect on the day's incredible art experiences. Visit a local Rome, GA restaurant for a celebratory dinner to mark the second-to-last evening of the trip. Share photos and memories from the day.

meals.breakfast: Hotel room breakfast with groceries (~$2–3)
meals.lunch: Pack snacks and a light lunch to eat near the museum — saves significant money compared to tourist-area restaurants (~$5–6 per person)
meals.dinner: Bella Roma or another Italian-themed restaurant in Rome, GA — celebrate the art-filled day with Italian cuisine (~$13–16 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Note: The Vatican Museums experience listed may be a local exhibition, virtual tour, or traveling exhibit rather than the actual Vatican in Rome, Italy — confirm the exact location and booking details with your experience provider. Book tickets well in advance regardless. This is the highlight art experience of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Rome, GA — revisit your favorite spot from the week for a peaceful farewell. Consider a sunrise walk along the Riverwalk or a quiet coffee on Broad Street. Pick up any local souvenirs from downtown shops — look for handmade or locally produced items to support local artists and keep costs low.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of La Quinta by Wyndham Rome (standard checkout is 11:00 AM — confirm with hotel). If time allows before departure, grab a final meal at a beloved local spot. Do a final sweep of the room for belongings. Head to the airport or begin your journey home.
day_by_day.evening: Travel home. Reflect on a wonderful week of art, food, history, and culture in Rome, GA — a surprisingly rich destination for budget-conscious travelers with eclectic interests.

meals.breakfast: Use up remaining grocery items from the hotel room — zero waste, zero cost
meals.lunch: Broad Street Baking Company or a local cafe for a final sit-down meal in Rome (~$10–13 per person)
meals.dinner: Airport food or travel snacks packed from grocery store items

day_by_day.notes: Total estimated daily food budget: $20–30 per person per day by using hotel room breakfasts, occasional picnics, and selecting mid-range local restaurants over tourist traps. Total 7-day food estimate: ~$140–210 per person. Biggest splurge is the Vatican Museums experience on Day 6 — worth every penny for art lovers. Overall trip is very achievable on a budget-conscious travel style.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 16:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Rome airport at 16:00 on Condor flight. Clear customs, collect luggage, and transfer to La Quinta by Wyndham Rome (15 Chateau Drive). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented. Take a leisurely stroll around the immediate neighborhood to shake off travel fatigue and get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk – Join a guided evening walk through the cobblestone streets of Trastevere, sampling supplì (fried rice balls), artichokes alla romana, local wines, and other Roman street bites. A perfect low-effort, high-reward introduction to Rome's culinary soul after a long travel day.

meals.breakfast: N/A – in transit
meals.lunch: N/A – in transit (grab something at the airport if needed)
meals.dinner: Covered largely by the Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk tastings. Supplement with a sit-down finish at Osteria der Belli in Trastevere – a mid-range trattoria known for cacio e pepe and Roman classics (~€20–30 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Book the Trastevere Evening Walk in advance as evening slots fill quickly in June. Wear comfortable walking shoes. June evenings are warm (~22–24°C) so light layers are sufficient. Keep luggage light for the transfer – Rome taxis from the airport run ~€48 flat rate to the city.

day_by_day.morning: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel – Start early (pre-booked 9:00 AM entry) to beat the crowds at one of the world's greatest art collections. Spend 2.5–3 hours exploring the Gallery of Maps, Raphael Rooms, and culminating in Michelangelo's breathtaking Sistine Chapel ceiling. Arrive 15 minutes before your slot.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Vatican, cross the Tiber to explore Castel Sant'Angelo and stroll along the scenic Lungotevere riverside promenade. Rest in the shade during the hottest part of the day (~2:00–3:30 PM) at a nearby café before heading to the Piazza Navona area to admire Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers and the surrounding Baroque architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through the historic centro storico. Visit the Pantheon (free evening exterior viewing), then explore the lively Campo de' Fiori market square as it transitions into evening aperitivo hour. Enjoy a Campari spritz at one of the piazza bars.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or grab a cornetto and cappuccino at a local bar near the hotel (~€3–5) – a true Roman morning ritual.
meals.lunch: Il Sorpasso near Prati (close to the Vatican) – a beloved mid-range spot for Roman sandwiches, suppli, and craft beer (~€15–20 per person).
meals.dinner: Ristorante Settimio all'Arancio near Piazza Navona – a classic Roman trattoria with excellent pasta alla gricia and saltimbocca (~€25–35 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Vatican Museums tickets MUST be pre-booked online (officialmuseumvatican.com). June is peak season – same-day tickets are nearly impossible. Dress code enforced: no bare shoulders or shorts above the knee for the Sistine Chapel. Carry a water bottle; June highs near 30°C make hydration essential.

day_by_day.morning: Borghese Gallery Art Tour – Visit this intimate yet world-class gallery housing Bernini's stunning sculptures (Apollo and Daphne, The Rape of Proserpina) and Caravaggio's dramatic paintings. Entry is strictly timed in 2-hour slots (book the 9:00 AM slot). The gallery is set within the beautiful Villa Borghese gardens.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the gallery, spend time strolling through the expansive Villa Borghese park – Rome's green lung. Rent a rowboat on the small lake (~€5/30 min) or simply relax under the umbrella pines. Descend via the Pincian Hill terrace for a panoramic view over Piazza del Popolo and Rome's rooftops. Explore Piazza del Popolo and the twin Baroque churches below.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Tridente neighborhood (Spanish Steps area). Climb the 135 steps of the Spanish Steps at sunset for golden-hour views over Rome. Browse the elegant Via Condotti and surrounding streets. Enjoy aperitivo hour in the stylish Prati or Tridente district.

meals.breakfast: Antico Caffè Greco near the Spanish Steps – one of Rome's oldest cafés, perfect for a cappuccino and pastry (~€5–8).
meals.lunch: Picnic in Villa Borghese gardens – pick up fresh bread, local cheeses, prosciutto, and fruit from a nearby alimentari (deli) near Via Veneto (~€10–15 per person). Ideal for a hot June afternoon.
meals.dinner: Osteria dell'Angelo in Prati – a beloved neighborhood gem known for authentic Roman cuisine like rigatoni con pajata and abbacchio (~€25–30 per person). Book ahead.

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery is one of Rome's most sought-after tickets – book at least 2–3 weeks in advance at galleriaborghese.it. Maximum 360 visitors per 2-hour slot. No re-entry permitted. The gallery is a 15-minute walk or short bus ride from the hotel area.

day_by_day.morning: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Archaeological Walk – Explore the ancient heart of the Roman Empire with a combined ticket covering the Colosseum, Roman Forum, and Palatine Hill. Start at the Forum (enter from Via Sacra) and walk where Julius Caesar, Augustus, and Cicero once tread. Climb Palatine Hill for sweeping views over the Forum and Circus Maximus below.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Colosseum (included in combined ticket) – the iconic amphitheater that once held 50,000 spectators. Afterward, cool down with a gelato and explore the Celio neighborhood's quieter streets. Visit the Basilica di San Clemente – a fascinating three-layered church revealing 2,000 years of Roman history underground.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Testaccio neighborhood – Rome's authentic working-class district. Explore the lively Saturday evening atmosphere around Monte Testaccio and the Pyramid of Cestius. This is Rome's best neighborhood for unpretentious, excellent food.

meals.breakfast: Bar San Calisto in Trastevere – a no-frills Roman bar beloved by locals for cheap, excellent coffee and cornetti (~€2–4).
meals.lunch: Terre e Domus near the Roman Forum – a mid-range restaurant with a terrace and solid Roman pasta dishes, convenient after the archaeological sites (~€20–28 per person).
meals.dinner: Flavio al Velavevodetto in Testaccio – a legendary trattoria built into Monte Testaccio (a hill made of ancient amphora shards), serving outstanding cacio e pepe and coda alla vaccinara (~€25–35 per person). Reserve ahead for Saturday.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book Colosseum/Forum/Palatine Hill combo tickets at coopculture.it to avoid 1–2 hour queues. Consider a 9:00 AM opening entry to beat the heat and crowds. Wear sturdy shoes – the Forum's cobblestones are uneven. Carry sun protection; the Forum has minimal shade and June sun is intense.

day_by_day.morning: Testaccio Market & Offal Food Tour – Dive deep into Rome's culinary soul at the Mercato Testaccio, the city's most authentic covered food market. A guided offal food tour introduces you to Roman quinto quarto (fifth quarter) cuisine: tripe, coda, and more, alongside fresh produce, artisan cheeses, and local street food stalls. Markets are especially vibrant on Sunday mornings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the Tiber to explore the Jewish Ghetto – one of Rome's most historically layered neighborhoods. Visit the Great Synagogue of Rome and the Portico d'Ottavia ruins. Stroll to the nearby Largo di Torre Argentina (where Julius Caesar was assassinated) and the cat sanctuary there. Continue to the Isola Tiberina (Tiber Island) for a peaceful afternoon walk.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Trastevere for a relaxed Sunday evening – the neighborhood is at its most atmospheric on summer Sunday nights with locals and visitors filling the piazzas. Enjoy live street music around Piazza di Santa Maria in Trastevere and the illuminated basilica facade.

meals.breakfast: Tastings at the Testaccio Market food tour cover morning snacks and bites – this IS breakfast and a late morning snack combined.
meals.lunch: Ba'Ghetto in the Jewish Ghetto – excellent Roman-Jewish cuisine including carciofi alla giudia (Jewish-style fried artichokes) and baccalà (~€22–30 per person).
meals.dinner: Da Enzo al 29 in Trastevere – a small, beloved trattoria with exceptional Roman classics like tonnarelli cacio e pepe and tiramisu (~€25–35 per person). Book well in advance – it's very popular.

day_by_day.notes: The Testaccio Market food tour typically runs 10:00 AM–12:30 PM on weekends. Book through a reputable local operator. Sunday in Rome means many churches are open for free (including Santa Maria in Trastevere) but some museums may have altered hours. The Jewish Ghetto area is particularly atmospheric on Sunday afternoons.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the lesser-visited but stunning Capitoline Museums – the world's oldest public museums, perched atop Capitoline Hill with extraordinary Roman sculptures (Marcus Aurelius equestrian statue, Capitoline Wolf) and a rooftop terrace with unbeatable Forum views. Spend 2–2.5 hours here for a deep dive into ancient Roman art.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the Aventine Hill – a quiet, leafy residential hill with two hidden gems: the Knights of Malta Keyhole (peek through for a perfectly framed view of St. Peter's dome) and the Orange Garden (Giardino degli Aranci) with panoramic views over Rome. A perfect, crowd-free afternoon escape. Descend to explore the Circus Maximus valley.
day_by_day.evening: Splurge slightly on a rooftop aperitivo experience – head to a rooftop bar in the centro storico for sunset drinks with views over Rome's domes and rooftops. Then explore the Monti neighborhood – Rome's hippest village-like district – for dinner and evening browsing of its artisan boutiques and wine bars.

meals.breakfast: Pasticceria Regoli near Piazza Vittorio – a historic Roman pastry shop famous for its maritozzo (cream-filled sweet bun), a Roman breakfast staple (~€4–6).
meals.lunch: Pizzarium Bonci near the Vatican/Prati area (worth the short trip) – Rome's most celebrated pizza al taglio (by the slice) shop by master baker Gabriele Bonci (~€10–15 per person).
meals.dinner: Ai Tre Scalini in Monti – a beloved wine bar and restaurant with excellent Roman dishes and an impressive wine list in a cozy setting (~€25–35 per person).

day_by_day.notes: The Knights of Malta Keyhole on Aventine Hill is free and one of Rome's most magical hidden experiences – go around 4:00–5:00 PM for best light. Capitoline Museums tickets available at museicapitolini.org. Monday can be quieter at many sites as some private galleries are closed, making it ideal for outdoor and archaeological exploration.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Rome – revisit a favorite neighborhood or tick off any remaining must-sees. Consider the Galleria Doria Pamphilj (a stunning private palazzo gallery with Velázquez's portrait of Pope Innocent X and Caravaggio works, often overlooked by tourists) near the Corso. Alternatively, spend a final peaceful morning at the Piazza Navona area, visiting Sant'Agnese in Agone church.
day_by_day.afternoon: Souvenir shopping and final wandering through the centro storico. Visit the Trevi Fountain (go early afternoon to avoid peak crowds) and toss a coin for your return. Stroll through the elegant Piazza di Spagna area one last time. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Rome – celebrate the end of a wonderful trip with a special meal. Head to the Pigneto or Prati neighborhood for a relaxed final dinner. Alternatively, enjoy a final gelato crawl comparing Rome's best gelaterias (Fatamorgana for creative flavors, Giolitti for classic).

meals.breakfast: Caffè Sant'Eustachio near the Pantheon – widely considered Rome's best espresso, a legendary institution. Try their gran caffè (~€3–5). Worth the short trip.
meals.lunch: Supplì Roma near Campo de' Fiori – the definitive Roman supplì (fried risotto balls) and casual Roman street food for a light, affordable final lunch (~€8–12 per person).
meals.dinner: Il Pagliaccio or a splurge at a mid-range restaurant of your choice in Prati – treat yourself to a memorable final Roman meal with wine. Alternatively, Osteria dell'Enoteca near Piazza del Popolo for excellent pasta and local Lazio wines (~€30–40 per person for a special farewell).

day_by_day.notes: Check hotel checkout time and arrange luggage storage if your departure is in the evening. The Trevi Fountain is best visited early morning or late afternoon to avoid the densest crowds. Keep some euros for last-minute gelato, espresso, and tips. Confirm return transport to the airport – allow at least 90 minutes travel time plus check-in.

Then visit St. Peter's Basilica and climb the dome for panoramic views over Rome (pre-book timed entry). Spend the late afternoon browsing the upscale boutiques along Via Cola di Rienzo.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel to refresh, then head to the historic center for an aperitivo at a rooftop bar such as Il Sorpasso or the terrace of Hotel Raphael for Campari spritzes with views of the Pantheon skyline.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel, then a mid-morning pastry at Caffè San Pietro near the Vatican – try the cornetto al pistacchio.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Il Sorpasso (Prati) – a beloved Roman bistro with excellent charcuterie boards, seasonal pasta, and natural wines. Ideal for a relaxed post-museum meal.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ristorante Il Matriciano (Prati) – a classic Roman institution near the Vatican, beloved for its bucatini all'amatriciana, abbacchio al forno, and warm, old-school atmosphere. Pair with a Cesanese del Piglio.

day_by_day.notes: Book Vatican Museums early-access tickets at least 4–6 weeks in advance – they sell out fast, especially in June. Dress code enforced at St. Peter's: covered shoulders and knees required. Carry a small bottle of water; June heat (≈30°C) can be intense.

day_by_day.morning: Borghese Gallery Art Tour – Take a private taxi or Uber to the Villa Borghese park for a premium guided tour of the Borghese Gallery (entry is strictly timed to 2-hour slots; book well in advance). Marvel at Bernini's Apollo and Daphne, The Rape of Proserpina, and Caravaggio's dramatic canvases in an intimate, uncrowded setting.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the gallery, enjoy a leisurely walk through the Villa Borghese gardens. Rent a rowboat on the lake or simply relax in the shade. Descend via the Spanish Steps to the Tridente district and explore the luxury shopping streets of Via Condotti (Bulgari, Valentino, Fendi) and Via del Babuino.
day_by_day.evening: Aperitivo hour at Stravinskij Bar inside the iconic Hotel de Russie – one of Rome's most glamorous garden bars, beloved by artists and celebrities. Sip a Negroni among jasmine-scented terraces.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Antico Caffè Greco on Via Condotti – Rome's oldest café (est. 1760), frequented by Keats, Byron, and Goethe. Order a cappuccino and maritozzo con la panna.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Ristorante Nino (Tridente) – a Florentine-Roman institution near the Spanish Steps, known for bistecca, ribollita, and an excellent Tuscan wine cellar. A favorite of the Roman intelligentsia.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Imàgo, the Michelin-starred rooftop restaurant of Hotel Hassler at the top of the Spanish Steps. Expect creative Italian haute cuisine with breathtaking panoramic views of Rome at dusk. Jacket recommended; reserve weeks ahead.

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery tickets must be reserved in advance – only 360 visitors per 2-hour slot. Arrive 15 minutes early or you forfeit entry. The gallery is closed Mondays. Wear comfortable shoes for the park walk and shopping.

day_by_day.morning: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Archaeological Walk – Join a premium small-group or private guided tour of the Roman Forum and Palatine Hill. Walk where Julius Caesar, Augustus, and Cicero once trod. A knowledgeable archaeologist-guide brings the ruins to life with vivid storytelling. Book a 9:00 AM slot to beat the midday heat.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Forum, visit the nearby Capitoline Museums (the world's oldest public museums) to see the original Marcus Aurelius equestrian statue, the Capitoline Wolf, and sweeping views over the Forum from the terrace. Then cool off with a gelato at Fatamorgana (artisan, gluten-free flavors) near Campo de' Fiori.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the atmospheric Campo de' Fiori market square at dusk (vendors pack up by afternoon, but the piazza buzzes with aperitivo life by evening). Stroll to the nearby Piazza Navona to admire Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers illuminated at night.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel, then a mid-morning espresso at Caffè Tazza d'Oro near the Pantheon – famous for its granita di caffè con panna in summer.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Ristorante Pierluigi (Campo de' Fiori area) – a beloved upscale seafood restaurant with a beautiful outdoor terrace. Try the spaghetti alle vongole and grilled branzino.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Il Pagliaccio – Rome's two-Michelin-starred gem near Campo de' Fiori. Chef Anthony Genovese crafts a boundary-pushing tasting menu blending Italian tradition with Asian influences. One of Rome's most extraordinary dining experiences. Reserve 4–6 weeks ahead.

day_by_day.notes: The Forum and Palatine Hill share a combined ticket; add the Colosseum for a full combo. Start early (9:00 AM) to avoid peak heat and crowds. Wear sunscreen and a hat. Il Pagliaccio requires formal attire and advance reservation.

day_by_day.morning: Testaccio Market & Offal Food Tour – Dive into Rome's most authentic culinary neighborhood with a premium guided food tour of the Mercato Testaccio. Taste supplì al telefono, porchetta, aged pecorino, artisanal pasta, and the neighborhood's famous offal specialties (trippa, coda). Your guide provides cultural context for each tasting.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the market, visit the nearby Non-Catholic Cemetery (Cimitero Acattolico) – a hauntingly beautiful garden cemetery where Keats and Shelley are buried, beloved by artists and writers. Then explore the Aventine Hill: visit the Knights of Malta keyhole (perfectly framing St. Peter's dome) and the serene Orange Garden (Giardino degli Aranci) with its panoramic city views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel for a rest during the hottest part of the afternoon. As the sun sets, take a private sunset boat tour on the Tiber River for a unique perspective of Rome's bridges and monuments from the water.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the hotel before the food tour (you'll be eating plenty on the tour).
meals.lunch: The Testaccio Food Tour serves as a substantial late-morning/lunch experience. Supplement with a sit-down lunch at Flavio al Velavevodetto – a legendary Testaccio trattoria carved into the Monte dei Cocci (ancient amphora hill), serving Roman classics like rigatoni con pajata and carciofi alla giudia.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ristorante Roscioli – a celebrated Roman deli-restaurant near Campo de' Fiori, famous for its extraordinary wine cellar (2,800+ labels), house-cured meats, and exceptional carbonara. Book well in advance.

day_by_day.notes: The Testaccio Market is open Tuesday–Sunday mornings; Sunday can be lively. Wear comfortable walking shoes. The Tiber boat tour should be pre-booked; sunset slots fill quickly in June. Roscioli is extremely popular – reserve at least 2–3 weeks ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Private Art Studio & Artisan Workshop – Arrange a private visit to a Roman artist's studio or a luxury artisan workshop (mosaic-making, fresco painting, or leather-bound bookbinding in the tradition of Roman craftsmen). Several ateliers near the historic center offer bespoke 2–3 hour sessions for premium guests. Alternatively, revisit the Pantheon at opening time (9:00 AM) for a contemplative, crowd-free experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the lesser-visited but stunning Palazzo Doria Pamphilj – a private aristocratic palace still owned by the Pamphilj family, housing Velázquez's portrait of Pope Innocent X and works by Caravaggio, Titian, and Raphael. The audio guide is narrated by a current family member. Afterward, wander the elegant Via del Corso for window shopping.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a classical music concert at a historic venue – Rome offers summer concerts in churches, courtyards, and villas throughout June. Options include concerts at the Oratorio del Gonfalone or outdoor performances at Villa Giulia. Dress elegantly for the occasion.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Pasticceria Regoli near the Esquilino – a historic Roman pastry shop (est. 1916) celebrated for its maritozzi con la panna and seasonal fruit tarts.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Osteria dell'Enoteca Corsi near the Pantheon – a charming, no-frills Roman lunch spot with a handwritten daily menu of traditional dishes like pasta e ceci and saltimbocca alla romana. Beloved by locals.
meals.dinner: Farewell-eve dinner at La Pergola – Rome's only three-Michelin-starred restaurant, perched atop the Rome Cavalieri hotel with sweeping panoramic views. Chef Heinz Beck's legendary tasting menu is a transcendent experience. Formal dress required; reserve 6–8 weeks in advance. This is the pinnacle of Roman fine dining.

day_by_day.notes: La Pergola is the crown jewel of Rome's dining scene – if you can only book one special dinner, make it this one. Palazzo Doria Pamphilj is closed Thursdays. The artisan workshop should be arranged through your hotel concierge at least 3–4 days in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Rome – Visit the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna (GNAM) in the Villa Borghese park for a quieter, world-class collection of 19th and 20th century Italian and international art (Klimt, Cézanne, Modigliani). Alternatively, spend a slow morning at the Piazza del Popolo: visit the twin baroque churches and the Church of Santa Maria del Popolo (Caravaggio's Conversion of Saint Paul).
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute luxury shopping along Via Condotti or Via Borgognona – pick up artisan gifts: a silk scarf from Battistoni, leather goods from Sermoneta Gloves, or bespoke stationery from Campo Marzio Design. Visit a high-end enoteca such as Trimani (Rome's oldest wine shop, est. 1821) to select bottles of Barolo or Brunello to bring home.
day_by_day.evening: Depart for the airport via pre-arranged private luxury transfer. Enjoy a final espresso at the airport lounge before your flight.

meals.breakfast: A slow, indulgent final breakfast at the hotel. Request a room-service spread or dine in the hotel restaurant with fresh pastries, fruit, and a proper cappuccino.
meals.lunch: Final lunch at Osteria Barberini near the Trevi Fountain – a refined Roman osteria with excellent cacio e pepe, artichoke dishes, and a curated wine list. Toss a coin in the Trevi Fountain afterward for good luck and a return to Rome.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the airport or in-flight, depending on departure time. Ask your hotel concierge to prepare a luxury picnic box with Roman specialties (prosciutto, aged pecorino, supplì, local wine) if your flight departs in the evening.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for check-in and security at Rome's Fiumicino (FCO) airport. Pre-arrange the return private transfer the night before. Confirm all luggage weight limits if purchasing wine or artisan goods. Keep a small amount of euros for tips and last-minute purchases.

query: Rome art and food trip, $2500, 7 days, June from Chicago
